issues.description: filters='*.exe' makes file picker useless on Linux/macOS
issues.detail: The conda executable browse dialog hardcodes filters='*.exe'. On Linux and macOS, conda/mamba/micromamba binaries have no extension. Users on those platforms will see an empty file list in the dialog and have to type the path. This is a Windows-ism leaking into a cross-platform app. Make the filter platform-conditional or drop it.

issues.description: validate_conda runs an arbitrary user-specified binary with no sanity check on intent
issues.detail: validate_conda() calls run_program(conda_executable, ['--version']) on whatever path the user typed and then string-matches 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' in the output. The substring match is loose enough that any binary printing those words anywhere in --version output passes. More concerning: this validation fires on every keystroke in the line edit if wired through the standard validate_callback path. That's running a subprocess on partial paths. Either gate the validation behind explicit user action (file picker selection, focus-out) or accept that this design is fine because validation is debounced -- but the current diff doesn't show that and create_lineedit's behavior matters here.

issues.description: Bytes decoded without specifying encoding will explode on non-UTF-8 locales
issues.detail: out.decode() with no argument uses utf-8 by default. On a Windows machine with a CP1252 console or a misconfigured Linux locale, this raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is then swallowed by the bare except. The function then returns False with the local 'valid' variable -- wait, the except returns False, so it returns False. Result: a perfectly valid conda binary on a non-UTF-8 system gets rejected with no diagnostic. Use out.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') or errors='ignore'.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows the actual failure
issues.detail: The try/except in validate_conda catches Exception and silently returns False. When a user's custom conda path doesn't work, they get 'not a valid Conda executable' with zero hint why. At minimum, log the exception. The kernel error message points users at this preference page -- when they get there and it rejects their path, they need to know why.

issues.description: os.access(path, os.X_OK) is not meaningful on Windows
issues.detail: On Windows, os.access with X_OK basically just checks existence. The real check is the file extension (.exe/.bat) and the OS will refuse to execute otherwise. Not wrong, just useless on the platform where filters='*.exe' is being applied. Minor.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() added to select_file with no explanation
issues.detail: select_file gains an edit.setFocus() call after setText. This is an unrelated UX tweak bundled into a feature patch. THREE-PATCHES: the conda-executable feature is one change, the create_browsefile validate_callback plumbing is arguably a second, and this setFocus tweak is a third. Either justify it in the commit message or pull it out.

issues.description: Existing custom_conda option is checked but the conda_path is also used unconditionally if non-empty -- inconsistent gating
issues.detail: In kernelspec.py: conda_exe = self.get_conf('conda_path') if self.get_conf('custom_conda') else None. Fine. But in confpage.py, conda_path's enabled state is bound to the checkbox -- good -- yet if a user once set a path, unchecked the box, the value persists in config. That's intentional (so re-enabling restores it) but worth a sanity check: does anything else in the codebase read conda_path without checking custom_conda? If yes, this is a latent bug. If no, fine. Spot-check before merging.

issues.description: Error message HTML in a string that may be displayed in non-HTML contexts
issues.detail:
The new SpyderKernelError message contains

and tags. If this message ever gets routed to a plain-text logger or console, users see literal tag markup. The old message was plain text. Verify SpyderKernelError's display path renders rich text everywhere it surfaces, or use plain text with newlines.

review.summary: The patch does one thing: adds a custom Conda executable preference so users with non-standard installs can point Spyder at it. Diff is scoped, readable, matches the surrounding confpage/widget conventions. The kernelspec fallback logic is straightforward. NEEDS-WORK on three concrete points: filters='*.exe' is platform-broken (Linux/macOS users will see an empty file dialog), validate_conda's out.decode() will UnicodeDecodeError on non-UTF-8 locales and silently reject valid binaries via the bare except, and the unrelated edit.setFocus() in select_file is a smuggled UX change that should be split out or justified. Taste-wise this is fine -- no gratuitous abstraction, the validation helper sits where it belongs in utils/conda.py, and the create_browsefile validate_callback plumbing is a reasonable widening of the existing API. Fix the cross-platform filter and the decode/error handling, split the setFocus change, and this lands.
